slides.title: Three moves for a better stovetop moka
slides.subtitle: Water, coffee, flame. One rule is the opposite of espresso.

slides.myth: Press the coffee down firmly, like you would for espresso.
slides.truth: Move 1: fill the basket generously, but don't press. Water needs an easy path through the grounds. Just level the top.

slides.title: Move 2: stop below the valve
slides.body: Pour cold water up to the safety valve's lower edge, not above it. The valve is a safety feature, so keep it uncovered.

slides.label: Move 3
slides.body: Set the flame to low and give it time. Great moka coffee is worth the wait.

slides.title: The whole routine
steps: Cold water up to the valve's lower edge.
Coffee in generously, level it, don't press.
Close the pot firmly. Flame on low.

slides.title: Water, coffee, flame, in that order
